notes: kb/Work PB1086/PB2099/PB2100/PB2103: Rule: 'Compilation of a program prototype definition or a function prototype definition generates information required for the external repository, as specified in 8.13, External repository.' (cite.py --check 10.6.3 -> OK 10.6.3 1)). 8.13: 'Whether the information is taken from a prototype or a definition, the information stored in the external repository about the signature of a program or a function is the same.' (OK 8.13); the update and flag mechanisms (OK 8.13) are --repository-update on|off and --repository-check on|off (DOC-A.1-66). VERIFIED: every outermost unit publishes its entry and its repository record (RepositoryPublication.EntryUnitsOf; DESIGN-external-repository 7.2) - a prototype is withheld only when a definition of the same externalized name in the SAME group already publishes the one signature (8.13: the same either way); a prototype compiled ALONE publishes its own. Re-probed on this branch: proto_only.cob (PROGRAM-ID. CGPO IS PROTOTYPE, LINKAGE 01 A PIC 9) compiled to CGPO.dll, then cgcall.cob (REPOSITORY. PROGRAM CGPO; CALL CGPO USING X with X PIC X(3)) is refused COBOL1688 against the published formal (the note's null signature that 'conforms' is gone). Witnesses: ExternalRepositoryResolutionTests.AProgramPrototypeCompiledAlone_..., AFunctionPrototypeCompiledAlone_... (published, and with update off found but unusable, REPO-8), APrototypeAndItsDefinitionInTwoUnits_AreComparedByLayout_NotByGroupingOrNames (a prototype and a definition of two units compare as one signature), pb2103_prototype_group_split_across_units; in-group udf_prototype and the pb894 goldens.
